The Green Mango Club is Chaweng's biggest and longest-running nightclub, an open-air venue on several levels at the beach end of Soi Green Mango. It is open every night, listed as 21:00 to 04:00 in 2026, entry is usually free, and you must be 20 or over with ID. It is almost empty before midnight and busiest from about 01:00 to 03:00; Saturday is the biggest night, and cocktails cost roughly 200–350 THB.

It is still operating in late 2026: guides updated in February, July and October 2026 list it as open nightly. Hours change with the season and the licence, so treat the times below as a guide and check on the night.

What it's like

The Green Mango has been part of Chaweng's nightlife for more than 20 years, and the lane is named after it. It is one large, mostly open-air compound built in a tree-house style: several bars, two main dance floors on different levels joined by wooden walkways, pool tables, big screens and lasers. Listings put its capacity at well over a thousand people.

It is a mainstream club, not an underground one. The area by the entrance plays hip-hop, R&B and chart hits; the main room plays EDM, house and singalong remixes with resident and visiting DJs. The crowd is young and international: backpackers, groups of friends, couples on a big night out and Thai clubbers at weekends.

Timing matters more than the night of the week. Arrive at 22:00 and you will find a near-empty room; most people come after midnight, once the beach bars and ARKbar's fire show have finished. From about 01:00 to 03:00 the dance floors are full, and on Saturdays in high season it is shoulder to shoulder. Ear plugs are worth bringing.

Vodka buckets are a fixture on the soi and are the cheapest way for a group to drink, but they are strong and easy to lose track of. Most bars on Soi Green Mango want cash, and foreign-card ATMs charge about 250 THB per withdrawal, so bring enough baht. Shops stop selling alcohol at midnight, but licensed clubs keep their own hours.

Tips and safety

  • ID: the drinking age is 20 and the door can check. Carry a copy of your passport photo page and leave the original in your hotel safe.
  • Your drink: the UK Foreign Office warns that drink spiking and drug-assisted sexual assault happen in Thai tourist areas, to both men and women, most often near bars late at night. Watch your drink being poured, never leave it and don't accept drinks from strangers.
  • Bills: pay per round rather than running a tab, and check for drinks you didn't order or a service charge that wasn't on the menu.
  • Touts: on the soi, touts sell "free entry" deals, party-boat seats and cheap Muay Thai tickets. You don't need them to get into the club; buy fight tickets at the stadium or from us.
  • Pockets: the soi is packed after midnight. Keep phones and wallets zipped away.
  • Drugs and vapes: Thailand's drug laws are severe, police carry out urine tests at party venues, and vapes are illegal for everyone, including tourists. Details: drugs and alcohol law on Samui.
  • The sea: the club backs onto Chaweng Beach. Don't swim after drinking, especially from October to December, when rip currents are common.
  • Help: Tourist Police 1155, police 191, ambulance 1669. Common tricks are on our Koh Samui scams page.

Who it suits, and who should go elsewhere

Good for: groups and couples who want a big, easy, free-entry night with familiar music; first-timers in Chaweng; anyone staying within walking distance of the soi.

Go elsewhere if: you want techno or underground electronic music (try Sound Club Samui on an event night, a few doors up the lane); you want a quiet drink (Fisherman's Village and the north-coast beach bars finish by midnight); you are under 20; or you want a sunset or pool party rather than a club (see Koh Samui beach clubs). Lamai's pubs and live bands suit an older crowd: Lamai nightlife.

Getting there and home

  • Walk: if you are staying in central Chaweng, walk. Turn off Chaweng Beach Road into Soi Green Mango and follow the lane towards the sea.
  • Grab: works well in Chaweng. Expect about 80–120 THB within Chaweng and 200–400 THB to Lamai or Bophut late at night, with longer waits and surge prices after 02:00 and in rain.
  • Taxis: wait on Chaweng Beach Road. A May 2026 crackdown told Samui taxis to use their meters, but in practice most still quote a fixed fare, so agree the price before you get in.
  • Songthaews: mostly stop by 20:00–22:00, so they are no use at 03:00.
  • Scooters: don't ride home. Police run checkpoints in Chaweng and on the ring road at night. The limit is 50 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood, or 20 mg for under-20s and anyone without a valid licence, which includes visitors riding without a motorcycle licence. Travel insurance won't pay for a drink-riding crash.

We arrange taxis and private drivers on WhatsApp for a pre-agreed price, including a pickup at the end of the night. Message us with your hotel and the time you want collecting. More options: getting around Koh Samui.
